newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Colly Cotton says to meet forecast.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Colly Cotton says to meet forecast.

text.p: Cotton producer and marketer Colly Cotton Ltd said on Thursday it expected to meet its prospectus forecast of a $21.4 million operating profit for the year to June 30, 1997.

"Directors believe the forecast will be achieved, while noting the variations in growing conditions since planting and that their effect on the yield and grade of the crop is yet to be fully realised," Colly said in a statement accompanying its first half results.
"Predominantly fine weather conditions throughout the upcoming harvest period are also essential," it added.
Colly Cotton, which floated on the Australian Stock Exchange last October, earlier announced an operating profit for the six months to December 31, 1996 of A$4.23 million.
Colly said a significant proportion of cotton industry profit emerges in the second half of the financial year, and the current result related to finalisation of the 1996 harvest.

The result reflected a lower than estimated average yield turnout on the second picking during the June 1996 harvest, and a fall in bales traded in its international marketing division due to a delay in starting its new operations in Dallas, Texas.
Unsold stock worth about A$400,000 from the 1996 season would be carried into the full year result.
Colly said recent rains were expected to delay the 1997 harvest in some areas by several weeks, but would not affect the company's export programme.
The rains had also enabled Colly to reduce farm costs for the 1997 season, and increased the expected availability of water in 1998, it said.
